dedupe_keys.name: cyber physical testbed for power system wide area measurement based control using open source software university of tennessee

description: This record describes a cyber-physical testbed for verifying and demonstrating wide-area measurement-based control of power systems, presented in a 2018 arXiv paper from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. The paper notes that simulation is crucial to understanding the dynamics and control of electric power systems while the underlying communication system has historically been ignored, and proposes a decoupled architecture that combines a differential algebraic equation based physical system simulator, a software-defined network, a scripting language environment for prototyping an energy management system and a control system, all integrated over industry-standard communication protocols and driven by streaming telemetry and phasor measurement unit data. The testbed is implemented with open-source packages managed by a Python dispatcher, and demonstrations show two wide-area controls, system separation control and hierarchical voltage control. Coverage is a laboratory testbed with two demonstrated controls. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; no repository link or licence is given in the abstract. Caveats: a research testbed. It suits testing of interactions between grid control and communication, and relates to the ANDES simulator catalogued here.
